52962-hugh-gwyeth-a-roundhead-cavalier.creator: Unknown
52962-hugh-gwyeth-a-roundhead-cavalier.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. of Everscombe manor house the ancient rooks were gravely wrangling. A faint morning breeze swept the green branches and, as the leaves stirred, the warm September sunlight smiting through fell in flakes of yellow on the dark flagstones of the terrace below.

arxiv-2104-00963.title: A new perspective on Wasserstein distances for kinetic problems Thanks: ETH Zürich, Department of Mathematics, Rämistrasse 101, 8092 Zürich, Switzerland. Email: mikaela.iacobelli@math.ethz.ch
arxiv-2104-00963.creator: Mikaela Iacobelli
arxiv-2104-00963.description: Abstract . We introduce a new class of Wasserstein-type distances specifically designed to tackle questions concerning stability and convergence to equilibria for kinetic equations. Thanks to these new distances, we improve some classical estimates by Loeper [ 49 ] and Dobrushin [ 16 ] on Vlasov-type equations, and we present an application to quasi-neutral limits. 1. Introduction 1.1.

arxiv-2106-10803.title: Qubit Heating Near a Hotspot
arxiv-2106-10803.creator: G. Kaplanek, C.P. Burgess, and R. Holman
arxiv-2106-10803.description: Abstract Effective theories describing black hole exteriors contain many open-system features due to the large number of gapless degrees of freedom that lie beyond reach across the horizon. A simple solvable Caldeira-Leggett type model of a quantum field interacting within a small area with many unmeasured thermal degrees of freedom was recently proposed in arXiv:2106.

arxiv-2204-05202.title: Perturbative region on non-Gaussian parameter space in single-field inflation
arxiv-2204-05202.creator: and Jun’ichi Yokoyama
arxiv-2204-05202.description: Abstract We calculate one-loop correction to the two-point functions of curvature perturbation in single-field inflation generated by cubic self-interaction. Incorporating the observed red-tilted spectrum of curvature perturbation, the relevant one-loop correction takes a finite value and inversely proportional to the spectral tilt.

arxiv-2206-05903.title: Geometrically Guided Integrated Gradients
arxiv-2206-05903.creator: Md Mahfuzur Rahman, Noah Lewis & Sergey Plis
arxiv-2206-05903.description: Abstract Interpretability methods for deep neural networks mainly focus on the sensitivity of the class score with respect to the original or perturbed input, usually measured using actual or modified gradients. Some methods also use a model-agnostic approach to understanding the rationale behind every prediction.

arxiv-2208-14349.title: WikiLink: an encyclopedia-based semantic network for design innovation
arxiv-2208-14349.creator: Haoyu Zuo, Qianzhi Jing, Tianqi Song, Huiting Liu, Lingyun Sun, Peter Childs, Liuqing Chen
arxiv-2208-14349.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Haoyu Zuo, Qianzhi Jing, Tianqi Song, Huiting Liu, Lingyun Sun, Peter Childs, Liuqing Chen. Data-driven design and innovation is a process to reuse and provide valuable and useful information. However, existing semantic networks for design innovation is built on data source restricted to technological and scientific information.

arxiv-2304-01122.title: Charge-density wave fluctuation driven composite order in the layered Kagome Metals
arxiv-2304-01122.creator: Alexei M. Tsvelik, Saheli Sarkar
arxiv-2304-01122.description: Abstract The newly discovered kagome metals AV 3 Sb 5 (A = K, Rb, Cs) offer an exciting route to study exotic phases arising due to interplay between electronic correlations and topology. Besides superconductivity, these materials exhibit a charge-density wave (CDW) phase occurring at around 100 K, whose origin still remains elusive.

arxiv-2401-11082.title: JWST observations of K2-18b can be explained by a gas-rich mini-Neptune with no habitable surface
arxiv-2401-11082.creator: Nicholas F. Wogan, Natasha E. Batalha, Kevin Zahnle, Joshua Krissansen-Totton, Shang-Min Tsai, Renyu Hu
arxiv-2401-11082.description: Abstract JWST recently measured the transmission spectrum of K2-18b, a habitable-zone sub-Neptune exoplanet, detecting CH 4 and CO 2 in its atmosphere. The discovery paper argued the data are best explained by a habitable “Hycean” world, consisting of a relatively thin H 2 -dominated atmosphere overlying a liquid water ocean.

arxiv-2407-06361.title: Concave Foliated Flag Structures and the SL 3 ​ ( ℝ ) \text{SL}_{3}(\mathbb{R}) Hitchin Component
arxiv-2407-06361.creator: Alexander Nolte and J. Maxwell Riestenberg
arxiv-2407-06361.description: Abstract . We give a geometric characterization of flag geometries associated to Hitchin representations in SL 3 ​ ( ℝ ) \mathrm{SL}_{3}(\mathbb{R}) . Our characterization is based on distinguished invariant foliations, similar to those studied by Guichard-Wienhard in PSL 4 ​ ( ℝ ) \mathrm{PSL}_{4}(\mathbb{R}) .

arxiv-2504-08138.title: Matrix concentration inequalities for dependent binary random variables Thanks: R.A.’s research was partially supported by The National Science Center, Poland, grant IMPRESS-U 2023/05/Y/ST1/00188
arxiv-2504-08138.creator: Radosław Adamczak, Ioannis Kavvadias
arxiv-2504-08138.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Radosław Adamczak, Ioannis Kavvadias. We prove Bernstein-type matrix concentration inequalities for linear combinations with matrix coefficients of binary random variables satisfying certain ℓ ∞ \ell_{\infty} -independence assumptions, complementing recent results by Kaufman, Kyng and Solda. For random variables with the Stochastic Covering Property or Strong Rayleigh Property we prove estimates for general functions satisfying certain direction aware matrix bounded difference inequalities, generalizing and strengthening earlier estimates by the first-named author and Polaczyk.

arxiv-2505-17733.title: The Pilot Corpus of the English Semantic Sketches
arxiv-2505-17733.creator: Maria Petrova, Maria Ponomareva, Alexandra Ivoylova
arxiv-2505-17733.description: Abstract The paper is devoted to the creation of the semantic sketches for English verbs. The pilot corpus consists of the English-Russian sketch pairs and is aimed to show what kind of contrastive studies the sketches help to conduct. Special attention is paid to the cross-language differences between the sketches with similar semantics.

arxiv-2509-19375.title: Uncertainty Quantification of Large Language Models using Approximate Bayesian Computation
arxiv-2509-19375.creator: Mridul Sharma, Adeetya Patel, Zaneta D’souza, Samira Abbasgholizadeh Rahimi, Siva Reddy, Sreenath Madathil
arxiv-2509-19375.description: Abstract Despite their widespread applications, Large Language Models (LLMs) often struggle to express uncertainty, posing a challenge for reliable deployment in high stakes and safety critical domains like clinical diagnostics. Existing standard baseline methods such as model logits and elicited probabilities produce overconfident and poorly calibrated estimates.

arxiv-2512-13144.title: Weight Space Correlation Analysis: Quantifying Feature Utilization in Deep Learning Models
arxiv-2512-13144.creator: Chun Kit Wong 1,2, Paraskevas Pegios 1,2, Nina Weng 1, Emilie Pi Fogtmann Sejer 3,4, Martin Grønnebæk Tolsgaard 3,4, Anders Nymark Christensen 1, Aasa Feragen 1,2
arxiv-2512-13144.description: Abstract Deep learning models in medical imaging are susceptible to shortcut learning, relying on confounding metadata (e.g., scanner model) that is often encoded in image embeddings. The crucial question is whether the model actively utilizes this encoded information for its final prediction.

pmc-10698279.title: Two-dimensional materials as sodium-ion battery anodes: The mass transfer and storage mechanisms of “fat” Na+
pmc-10698279.creator: Yuan Shao, Yong Zhang, Na Jiang, Yuhan Hao, Keqi Qu, You Zeng, Ziqiang Liu, Xuejun Lu, Ying Li, Qi Yang, Jieshan Qiu
pmc-10698279.description: SummarySodium-ion batteries (SIBs) with abundant resource and high safety are attracting intensive interest from both research and industry communities in meeting the ever-increasing energy demands. Despite the rapid advance of SIBs, it is difficult yet necessary to enhance the cycling and rate performance at anode due to the sluggish kinetics of “fat” Na+.

pmc-11400956.title: Identifying and resolving conflict in mobile application features through contradictory feedback analysis
pmc-11400956.creator: Ishaya Gambo, Rhodes Massenon, Roseline Oluwaseun Ogundokun, Saurabh Agarwal, Wooguil Pak
pmc-11400956.description: As mobile applications proliferate and user feedback becomes abundant, the task of identifying and resolving conflicts among application features is crucial for delivering satisfactory user experiences. This research, motivated to align application development with user preferences, introduces a novel methodology that leverages advanced Natural Language Processing techniques.

pmc-11615408.title: Co‐treatment with erythropoietin derived HBSP and caspase‐3 siRNA: A promising approach to prevent fibrosis after acute kidney injury
pmc-11615408.creator: Yuanyuan Wu, Yanan Wang, Fei Chen, Cheng Han, Lili Huang, Wenli Sai, Yaping Fan, Nigel J. Brunskill, Bin Yang
pmc-11615408.description: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a risk factor of chronic kidney disease, without specific treatment. This study investigated the effect of co‐treatment using erythropoietin‐derived helix B surface peptide (HBSP) and caspase‐3 small interfering RNA (CASP3siRNA) on preventing fibrosis post AKI in order to achieve better efficacy by different action mechanisms.

pmc-13318284.title: Causal Relationship Between Gut Microbiota and Female Infertility: A Bidirectional Mendelian Randomization Analysis
pmc-13318284.creator: Qiuying Gan, Lidan Liu, Bo Liu, Mujun Li
pmc-13318284.description: ObjectiveThis study aims to investigate the causal relationship between gut microbiota and female infertility using a Mendelian randomization (MR) approach.MethodsA bidirectional MR analysis was conducted using genome-wide association study (GWAS) data from European populations. Genetic variants (SNPs) linked to 473 bacterial species were used as instrumental variables.

pmc-13560032.title: Dynamic changes and roles of LYVE-1 during lipopolysaccharide-induced ALI/ARDS in mice
pmc-13560032.creator: Shuntaro Matsunaga, Shinnosuke Takamori, Shen Lin, Chen Man, Yukie Mizuta, Sayoko Narahara, Takahito Kawano, Masaharu Murata, Tomohiko Akahoshi
pmc-13560032.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Highlights•LYVE-1 expression dynamically changes in acute lung injury.•LYVE-1 expression exceeds basal levels during the resolution phase.•Pharmacologic LYVE-1 blockade exacerbates lung injury in LPS-induced ARDS.•M2 macrophages express LYVE-1 during the ARDS resolution phase.Keywords: LYVE-1, Acute lung injury, ARDS, M2 macrophage Introduction Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is characterized by severe hypoxemia due to non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema with excessive alveolar-capillary permeability and poor prognosis [[1], [2], [3]].

pmc-13666567.title: The basal ganglia and the epilepsies
pmc-13666567.creator: Willian Lazarini‐Lopes, Logan Perry, Patrick A Forcelli
pmc-13666567.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The basal ganglia are an evolutionarily conserved neural circuit best known for the selection and sequencing of voluntary movement. Increasing evidence, however, indicates that these structures also play an important role in regulating pathological brain states, including seizures. Early pharmacological and lesion studies demonstrated that manipulation of basal ganglia output nuclei, particularly the substantia nigra pars reticulata, profoundly alters seizure susceptibility across multiple experimental models.
